headline: Bitcoin is back above $80,000 as US stocks rally after the Democrats' sweep of Congress, while a French bank confirms the cyberattack behind a suspected $133M crypto theft.

market.asOf: Read from the CoinDesk price ticker about 16:10 UTC Wed 4 Nov (23:10 Bangkok); changes are over 24 hours. For current prices, use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: Not read this run: the Fear & Greed source could not be opened. The last reading on this page was 26 (Fear) on the Alternative.me index at 11:54 UTC 4 Nov.

stories.title: Bitcoin climbs back above $80,000 as stocks rally after the midterms
stories.summary: Bitcoin dropped below $76,000 overnight as election results came in, then kept climbing once Wall Street opened, passing $80,500. Falling oil prices helped risk assets. Money is still leaving US bitcoin funds, so the rebound has not yet been backed by fresh ETF buying.
points: Bitcoin fell to about $75,600 and then recovered, per CoinDesk.
Bitcoin passed $80,500 at the Wall Street open, up more than 4% on the day, per Cointelegraph (15:29 UTC).
US oil (WTI) fell below $93 a barrel, down as much as 11.9% for the week, per Cointelegraph.
US spot bitcoin ETFs had a net outflow of $115.6M on 3 Nov and spot ether ETFs lost $85.3M, per LiveBitcoinNews citing Farside.
CoinDesk's DeFi Select Index rose about 5%, while TRUMP fell 7.1% and WLFI 5%, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: Democrats control Congress: what it means for crypto rules
stories.summary: Democrats now control both chambers of Congress. Analysts quoted by CoinDesk expect a tougher next draft of the stalled CLARITY market-structure bill, and Tagus Capital says altcoins and DeFi stay more exposed to regulatory risk than bitcoin.
points: The CLARITY Act market-structure bill stalled in the Senate on a 49-50 vote in September, per CoinDesk.
TransFi's Raj Kamal expects "tougher consumer safeguards and stablecoin yield limits" in the next CLARITY Act draft, per CoinDesk.
Tagus Capital says altcoins and DeFi platforms "stay vulnerable to regulatory execution risk" under the new Congress, per CoinDesk.
The GENIUS stablecoin law takes effect on 18 January 2027 alongside the OCC's final rule, per CoinDesk.

sources.label: CoinDesk Daybook: analysts react to the new blue Congress

stories.title: French bank confirms a cyberattack behind a suspected $133M crypto theft
stories.summary: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirmed it suffered a cyberattack that enabled fraudulent transactions, but has not confirmed investigator ZachXBT's estimate of over $133M. It comes days after Binance's multibillion-dollar breach, which Binance says began with a fake job interview.
points: The bank said customer assets were not affected and the incident was contained; the amount is still being assessed, per FinanceFeeds.
ZachXBT reported over $106M of suspicious withdrawals on 2 Nov and raised it above $133M on 3 Nov, per FinanceFeeds.
Bitquery traced about $108.8M in USDC withdrawn over about 21 hours from accounts at Kraken, Crypto.com and OKX, per FinanceFeeds.
Binance says its breach started with a fake job interview that infected an engineer's laptop, per Fox Business.
Coinbase says its customers were not affected by the Binance breach, per crypto.news.
